docs.title: pytest-concurrency
docs.text: A pytest plugin for parallel test execution with configurable concurrency.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Parallel test execution — run tests concurrently using multiple workers
  • Thread-safe pytest internals — patches pytest's internal state for thread isolation
  • Optional Allure integration — works with allure-pytest when installed
  • Auto-detection — automatically use CPU count with --workers auto
  • Round-robin distribution — balanced test load across workers

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install
pip install pytest-concurrency

# Run tests with 4 parallel workers
pytest --workers 4

# Auto-detect CPU cores
pytest --workers auto

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: The plugin patches pytest internals (SetupState, FixtureDef, os.environ) to make them thread-local, enabling safe parallel execution. Tests are distributed across workers using a round-robin algorithm, with parametrized tests kept together to avoid setup/teardown conflicts.

docs.title: get_workers_count
docs.text:
def get_workers_count(
    config: Config,
    arg_name: str,
    default: int = DEFAULT_WORKERS_COUNT
) -> int

Determine the number of workers from pytest config.

Parameters:

Name Type Description config Config pytest configuration object arg_name str Argument name to query default int Default count when auto-detection fails (default: 1)

Returns: int — Number of workers

Behavior:

  • If value is an integer — returns it directly
  • If value is "auto" — returns os.cpu_count() or default if CPU count is unavailable

Example:

from pytest_concurrency.tools import get_workers_count
from _pytest.config import Config

workers = get_workers_count(config, "workers", default=2)

docs.title: pytest_addoption
docs.text:
Registers the plugin's command-line options:

  • --workers — Number of parallel workers (int or "auto")
  • --worker-timeout — Timeout for worker threads (seconds)

docs.title: pytest_runtestloop
docs.text:
Custom test execution loop that:

  1. Creates test suites for each worker
  2. Spawns worker threads
  3. Runs tests in parallel
  4. Waits for completion with timeout

docs.title: Patching Functions
docs.text:
Internal

pytest-concurrency patches internal pytest classes at module level when the plugin is enabled. Do not call these directly.

Function Module Purpose patch_os system.py Makes os.environ thread-local patch_pytest_runner runner.py Makes SetupState thread-local patch_pytest_fixtures fixtures.py Makes FixtureDef thread-local patch_allure allure.py Makes Allure classes thread-local (optional)

docs.title: Command-Line Options
docs.text:
Plugin activation

The plugin enables parallel execution only when --workers is passed on the command line or PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS is set in the environment. Passing --worker-timeout (or setting PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKER_TIMEOUT) alone does not activate the plugin — tests run sequentially.

docs.title: --workers
docs.text:
Number of parallel workers for test execution.

pytest --workers 4
pytest --workers auto  # Uses CPU count

Default: Plugin disabled (sequential execution)

Values:

Value Description N (int) Run with exactly N workers auto Auto-detect using os.cpu_count()

docs.title: --worker-timeout
docs.text:
Timeout in seconds for how long the main thread waits for each worker thread to finish. Once the timeout elapses, the plugin stops waiting — the test run is not marked as failed, and tests still running in that worker may not report results.

pytest --workers 4 --worker-timeout 300

Default: None (wait indefinitely)

docs.title: PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS
docs.text:
Enable parallel execution and set worker count.

export PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS=4
pytest  # Runs with 4 workers

Values: Same as --workers CLI option

docs.title: PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKER_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Set worker timeout via environment.

export PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKER_TIMEOUT=300
pytest  # Workers timeout after 5 minutes

docs.title: Priority
docs.text:
CLI options take precedence over environment variables:

  1. --workers CLI option
  2. PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS environment variable
  3. Plugin disabled (sequential execution)

docs.title: Test Distribution
docs.text:
Tests are distributed using round-robin algorithm:

  1. All tests are sorted by nodeid
  2. Parametrized tests with the same module.class.function are grouped together
  3. Groups are distributed across workers in round-robin fashion

This ensures:

  • Balanced load across workers
  • Setup/teardown consistency for parametrized tests
  • Deterministic distribution (same tests always go to same worker)

docs.title: Basic Parallel Execution
docs.text:
# Run tests with 4 parallel workers
pytest --workers 4 tests/

docs.title: Auto-Detect CPU Count
docs.text:
# Automatically use all available CPUs
pytest --workers auto

docs.title: Via Environment Variable
docs.text:
# Set workers via environment (useful for CI)
export PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS=4
pytest

docs.title: With Timeout
docs.text:
# Stop waiting for workers if they don't finish within 5 minutes
pytest --workers 4 --worker-timeout 300

After the timeout elapses, the plugin stops waiting for worker threads — the test run itself is not marked as failed, and tests still running in those workers may not report results.

docs.text:

  run: pytest --worker-timeout 600
  env:
    PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS: ${{ vars.PARALLEL_WORKERS || 'auto' }}

docs.text:
test:
  script:
    - pytest --workers ${CI_PARALLELISM:-auto}

docs.title: With Coverage
docs.text:
# Works with pytest-cov
pytest --workers 4 --cov=myapp --cov-report=term-missing

docs.title: With Allure Reports
docs.text:
# Install allure-pytest first
pip install allure-pytest pytest-concurrency

# Run with parallel execution and Allure
pytest --workers 4 --alluredir=allure-results

Note

pytest-concurrency automatically patches Allure classes for thread-safety when allure-pytest is installed.

docs.title: Good: Stateless Tests
docs.text:
def test_pure_function():
    # Pure functions are safe
    result = calculate_something(42)
    assert result == expected_value

def test_with_fixtures(db_session):
    # Fixtures are thread-local when patched
    assert db_session.query(User).count() >= 0

docs.title: Avoid: Shared Mutable State
docs.text:
# BAD: Shared mutable state
shared_list = []

def test_appends_to_list():
    shared_list.append(1)  # Race condition!
    assert len(shared_list) == 1

docs.title: Fix: Thread-Local Storage
docs.text:
import threading

# GOOD: Thread-local state
local_data = threading.local()

def test_with_thread_local():
    local_data.value = 42
    assert local_data.value == 42

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install pytest-concurrency

docs.title: Enable Parallel Execution
docs.text:
# Run with 4 workers
pytest --workers 4

# Auto-detect CPU count
pytest --workers auto

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
You can also configure workers via environment variable:

PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS=4 pytest

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When --workers is provided or PYTEST_CONCURRENCY_WORKERS is set, the plugin:

  1. Patches pytest internals — makes SetupState, FixtureDef, and os.environ thread-local
  2. Collects all tests — standard pytest collection
  3. Groups parametrized tests — keeps same test function with different params together
  4. Distributes across workers — round-robin assignment for balanced load
  5. Runs in parallel threads — each worker executes its test suite

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+
  • pytest 7.0+
  • gevent and pytest-gevent (required, installed automatically with the plugin)
  • Optional: allure-pytest for Allure integration

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Tests must be thread-safe (no shared mutable state)
  • Fixtures should not rely on process-level state
  • Some pytest plugins may be incompatible with threading
